links.outcome: Inter-rater reliability among psychiatrists rating LLM mental health responses
links.effect: Inter-rater reliability was consistently poor (ICC 0.087-0.295), below acceptable thresholds; one factor had Krippendorff's alpha -0.203; disagreement highest on suicide and self-harm items.
links.quote: Despite similar training and shared instructions, inter-rater reliability was consistently poor ($ICC$ $0.087$--$0.295$), falling below thresholds considered acceptable for consequential assessment.

unlisted_practices: Preserving and learning from expert disagreement rather than consensus-based aggregation of expert labels in reward modeling and safety evaluation

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the validity and reliability of expert clinical evaluation / human feedback rubrics as a safeguarding and safety testing practice for mental health LLM outputs.

primary.practice: expert human feedback and rater aggregation for safety evaluation
